answer: An agent economy can require every voting identity to lock a fixed bond for 90 days, with one vote per bonded identity. Whether an agent calls itself quartz or sable, each new vertex in the voting network needs its own deposit; the same funds cannot back two identities at once. An attacker seeking 1,000 votes must therefore immobilize 1,000 bonds, paying the financing cost and losing access to that capital for the full term.
